title: Dynamic kernel orchestration for multi-precision runtime paths
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We want the runtime to automatically pick the best execution path (FP16, FP8, INT8) per request and per-layer where appropriate to minimize cost while keeping model quality within defined tolerances. Existing components (kernel dispatcher, quant profiles, and offline calibration tooling) are partially implemented, but we lack a unified orchestration that composes: 1) quantization profile metadata (per-layer scale / clipping), 2) a runtime kernel capability matrix, 3) fast on-CPU decision logic for dispatch, and 4) integrated accuracy validation and rollback guards.

Goal: Implement a deterministic, low-overhead orchestration layer that: (a) selects kernel variants at runtime for mixed-precision execution, (b) supports per-model and per-customer quantization profiles, (c) integrates calibration results (offline and online) to update dispatch rules, and (d) provides telemetry and automatic fallback to FP16 when accuracy thresholds are violated.

Scope: This ticket covers the orchestration/dispatch logic and the associated validation workflow (calibration ingestion, offline accuracy sweep, canary rollout policy). Kernel implementations themselves are covered in kernel teams (separate PRs). This ticket will add the decision API, configuration format, runtime check-points, and the validation pipeline glue.

Key design decisions to make here: 1) representation for precision paths (layer ranges vs named blocks), 2) frequency of online calibration refresh (per-deployment, hourly, or on-change), 3) how to model acceptable degradation (absolute delta vs relative metric), and 4) deterministic tie-breaking when multiple kernels are compatible.

Success metrics: reduce token CPU/GPU cost by target while keeping held-out evaluation metrics within tolerance (see Test Plan).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Runtime dispatch selects mixed-precision kernels according to a quant profile manifest and logs the chosen path.
2) When a new calibration artifact is uploaded, the orchestration re-evaluates paths and marks candidate paths as "ready-for-canary" or "rejected" based on accuracy sweep.
3) Canary rollout (1% traffic) executes candidate mixed-precision path for at least 50k tokens without exceeding accuracy regression thresholds.
4) Automatic fallback to FP16 occurs if runtime monitors detect regression exceeding configured thresholds or if kernel errors are observed.
5) End-to-end tests (unit + integration + perf) are added and pass in CI.
tasks: Define quant profile manifest schema and add fields for per-layer scale, calibration timestamp, and confidence score.
Implement dispatcher component: accepts a model id + input metadata and returns kernel path (FP16/FP8/INT8) and per-layer overrides.
Add fast runtime checks: kernel capability bitset, model pinned profiles, and token-length heuristics to avoid slow paths for short sequences.
Glue validation pipeline: intake calibration artifacts, run offline accuracy sweeps against calibrated eval sets, produce pass/fail and recommended fallback plan.
Implement canary rollout logic and metric instrumentation hooks (accuracy deltas, per-token latency, kernel-error rates).
Create autoscale guard rails: if INT8/FP8 path reduces throughput below SLO, mark as not-eligible for production routing.
Add integration tests: mixed precision correctness against FP16 baseline for 5 different model families and 3 sequence length distributions.
Documentation: update runtime API docs, Console rollout UI text, and runbook for accuracy regression incidents.
test_plan:
Calibration datasets: use s3://redwood-evals/quant-calib/{model_family}/calib-1M.jsonl (representative prompts) and s3://redwood-evals/quant-eval/{model_family}/heldout-200k.jsonl for accuracy sweep.

Offline validation: run top-5 candidate precision paths per model and measure: delta-perplexity, token-likelihood KL, and downstream task accuracy (where available). Define thresholds: delta-perplexity <= 0.8%, KL <= 1.2%, downstream accuracy drop <= 0.5% absolute.

Canary rollout: route 1% traffic for 72 hours or 50k tokens, whichever comes later. Monitor rolling 1-hour and 6-hour windows. Alert conditions: accuracy metric breach, kernel-native errors > 0.1%, p95 latency > SLO + 30%.

Production rollout: only after canary passes. Continuous monitoring will compute a quality score; if score drops below 0.95 of baseline for 3 consecutive windows, trigger automated rollback to FP16 path.
risks_mitigation:
Risk: calibration overfits to small eval sets -> mitigate by using diverse multi-domain evals and confidence scoring for calibration artifacts.
Risk: dispatch overhead adds latency -> implement dispatch as a few branchless checks with cached bitsets and micro-benchmarks before merging.
Risk: silent quality regressions in long-tail prompts -> include drift detection (token-likelihood drift) and conservative default: prefer FP16 for short sequences and safety-critical customers.
